key_insight: A physics-constrained, multi-fidelity turbulence model can be trained at low Reynolds number and then extrapolated to higher Reynolds numbers with formal cost scaling of O(log(Re)) under stated wall-bounded-flow assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This offers a pathway toward cheaper yet accurate CFD predictions for engineering turbulence, especially when direct high-fidelity simulation becomes prohibitively expensive at high Reynolds number.
method: Augment the Spalart–Allmaras RANS model using field inversion and machine learning.
Constrain the learned correction to preserve the law of the wall.
Train at affordable low-Re cases and deploy the model to higher-Re flows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful transfer from channel flow at Re_tau=1000 to Re_tau=5200 and from periodic hill training at Re_b=5600 to tests at Re_b=10595, 19000, and 37000, with improved separation/recovery behavior and low RMSE.
watch_item: The claimed log(Re) cost and extrapolation depend on specific assumptions such as mean-flow-aligned grids, fixed spanwise resolution, and steady-solver scaling, so performance may not generalize outside these conditions.
paper_title: A formal log(Re)-cost framework for the engineering turbulence problem
